results.text: Breathe in. Ripe fruit, cured meats, fish on ice: this iron-and-glass hall from 1888 still feeds Gràcia, a neighbourhood that was its own town until 1897. Look along the counters and notice how food is weighed, wrapped by hand and talked over. Many stallholders know their customers by name, because this is where real neighbours do their everyday shopping. If you'd like a taste, some local cheese or a paper cone of olives makes a perfect snack for your walk. Greet the stallholder with a warm bon dia, and enjoy being a guest in Gràcia's pantry.

results.text: Camp Nou simply means "new field" in Catalan, a modest name for one of the most famous stadiums on earth. Look at the great curve of the stands rising in front of you. When it opened in 1957, it replaced the club's older, smaller ground nearby, here in Les Corts. FC Barcelona's motto is "Més que un club", more than a club, and for generations this place has carried Catalan identity, pride and memory alongside the football. Les Corts is a real neighbourhood where families live, so keep your voice low as you wander its streets.

results.text: Look around at the balconies framing this square. Behind those railings, people are living their everyday lives, and many of them treat the square below as an extension of home. Gràcia's neighbours have met here for generations. Notice who's around you: friends catching up after work, a drink in the afternoon sun, conversations that drift from table to table. Beneath your feet, a bomb shelter was dug during the Spanish Civil War. Today, the local ritual is simpler: sit, linger, chat. And as evening falls, do as the neighbours do, and keep your voice low.

results.text: Notice how the whole façade shimmers, like the surface of water catching the light. It's covered in fragments of coloured glass and ceramic, a mosaic technique Gaudí loved. This is Antoni Gaudí at his most playful, a master of Catalan Modernisme who took an ordinary house and remade it as a work of art. Now look up at the roof, curved like a dragon's scaly back, pierced by a tower that suggests the sword of Sant Jordi. The balconies look like skulls, the columns like bones. Enjoy it quietly. People live and work all along this street.
